question: Momentum of a body is defined to be the product of its:
solution:
The correct answer is __**mass and velocity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Momentum** of a body is defined to be the product of its mass and velocity.
 
• It is the property of a moving body.
 
• SI unit is **kg×m/s.**
 
• Dimension: **MLT−1**
 
• p = mv; p = momentum, m = mass, and v = velocity
 
• So the momentum of a body depends upon both mass and velocity of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Linear momentum: The product of mass and velocity is known as linear momentum.
 
• Angular Momentum (L): It is a property of a body in rotational motion.
 
 
• The moment of linear momentum is known as angular momentum.
